# Limiter skip log prints an impossible ratio when the reserve is in use

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Problem

`SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` logs the rejection ratio as
`len(window)/max_rpm`, but with the free-tier reserve
(`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) the per-caller cap can be lower than the number of
entries already in the window, producing log lines that look like a bug:

```
WARNING - Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 10/7 requests in 60s window
WARNING - Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=7 reserve=3 ...
```

The `10` is the count in the window (including slots taken by in-progress
sessions), the `7` is the cap applied to this new-session request. Operators and
log analyses read `10/7` as an arithmetic error.

## Desired change

Make the message self-describing, e.g.:

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: window=10 cap=7 (reserve in use) requests in 60s window
```

Keep the emitted fields parseable (stable `key=value` tokens) so the
proxy-usage / budget-effectiveness analyses can extract `window=` and `cap=`
instead of inferring them from provider config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rejection log line names both the in-window count and the cap applied to
  the rejected request, with no value that can read as `count/cap` confusion.
- A unit test asserts the emitted message contains `window=`, `cap=` and the
  correct numbers for (a) a plain over-limit rejection and (b) a
  reserve-limited rejection (cap < window count).
- No behaviour change: only the message text (and any consumed parse) changes;
  full project test suite passes.
- Stale references quoting the old `N/M requests in Ns window` wording are
  updated to the new format (see Affected references).

## Implementation notes

- The limiter only knows the cap it was handed (`effective_limit`); it does not
  know *why* that cap is below the configured `rate_limit_rpm`. A
  `(reserve in use)` annotation therefore requires the caller
  (`proxy/provider_budget.py`) to pass context, and is optional — the required,
  parseable fields are `window=` and `cap=`.
- If extra context is passed, prefer a stable token over prose so the
  `key=value` convention used by the companion `Provider budget exhausted`
  line is preserved (e.g. `cap=7 reserve=3`, not `(reserve in use)`).
- Test-first: add the message assertions to `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
  (plain over-limit case and `cap < window` case) before changing the format
  string.

## Affected references

- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py` — the format string and `logger.warning` call.
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py` — unit tests asserting the message fields.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` — comment quoting the old
  `13/11 requests in 60s window` wording.
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md` — same quoted wording.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md`

# Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want **one** authoritative description of the provider
fallback model — every knob that shapes a chain, the layer it applies at
(provider entry / model / server), and the order those layers win in — so I can
answer "how do I control X for model Y?" without reading `provider.py`, and so
new controls (e.g. per-model budget knobs, `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) slot into a
documented contract instead of inventing a new shape.

Low priority: documentation/consolidation only, no behaviour change.

## Current state (fragmented)

Fallback behaviour is described in five places that have drifted apart:
`proxy/config.yaml` header comments, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`,
`proxy/docs/routing.md` and inline code comments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` /
`provider_budget.py`. The knobs themselves are spread across three layers with
no single statement of precedence:

| Layer | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Provider entry | `rate_limit_rpm`, `available_times`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `forward_session_headers`, `api`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | per-entry, order defines chain position |
| Model (`models.<name>`) | `providers` list order, `aliases`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | one model key → one chain, shared by all aliases |
| Server (`server.*`) | `provider_cooldown_seconds`, `sibling_fallback_*`, `chain_hold_*`, `upstream_*`, `provider_rate_limit_*`, `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`, `max_retry_after_seconds` | global; some are inherited-only across mode overlays |
| Mode overlay | `config-fast.yaml`, `config-cheap.yaml` | lists replace wholesale; other values replace; only diffs declared |
| Runtime | cooldowns, usage-limit quarantine, stall circuit breaker, affinity records, budget windows | in-memory + `proxy/provider-state.json` |

Cross-cutting semantics that are easy to get wrong and belong in one place:
failure-domain grouping (shared endpoint+model), per-account vs per-endpoint
exclusion, time windows (`available_times`), the free-tier budget gate
(`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) including the reserve and
affinity, chain-hold retry cycles, sibling-fallback circuit breaker,
mode grandfathering, and which of these reset on proxy restart (in-memory vs
persisted).

## Desired change

1. A single reference document (e.g. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md`)
   covering: chain resolution order, every knob with its layer + default +
   precedence, the failure/cooldown/quarantine taxonomies, quota/budget gating,
   mode overlays and grandfathering, and what is persisted vs in-memory.
2. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to it instead of duplicating
   the detail (keep short, task-focused sections there).
3. A short "inconsistencies / gaps" section recording anything found while
   writing it (knobs only available globally, provider lists duplicated in the
   fast overlay, budget gating only on one entry, etc.) — recorded as
   `discovered-from` work items rather than fixed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` exists and states, for every
   fallback-related knob: name, layer, default, precedence, and the behaviour it
   controls — verified against the code paths that read it (no invented values).
2. A precedence table covers entry > model (where applicable) > server >
   built-in default, including the mode-overlay merge rule (lists replace,
   scalars replace, dicts merge) and the `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` inheritance
   contract.
3. The persistence section distinguishes state that survives a restart
   (`provider-state.json`, grandfathered bindings) from in-memory state
   (cooldowns, stall breaker, affinity, budget windows).
4. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to the new document and no
   longer contradict it.
5. Every inconsistency found is either fixed by a linked `discovered-from` item
   or explicitly recorded as accepted.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments where a pointer to the new document replaces duplicated prose.
7. Full project test suite passes (documentation-only change must not perturb
   behaviour).

## Constraints

- Documentation/analysis only: no behaviour, config-value or code-path changes in
  this item.
- Do not duplicate the new budget-gate material — reference
  `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` / `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` and the per-model controls item
  (`LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) rather than restating their designs.
- UK English, Markdown, no secrets (reference API keys by env-var name only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` — new reference document.
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — link + trim
  duplicated material.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — header comments point at the document.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — verify claims;
  replace duplicated comments with pointers only where clearly redundant.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV` — per-model budget knobs (the contract this document
  should describe once it lands).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — the free-tier budget gate,
  reserve and wait cap.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — whether `rate_limit_rpm` should be raised.
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` — header-derived budgeting.
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — free tier restricted to cheap mode.

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want the client-side bridge to log one line per
captured compaction signal and one line per reshape attempt, so that a
loaded-but-idle extension (bridge installed, no signal ever arrives) is
distinguishable from a broken one (signal arrived, bridge did nothing) —
satisfying AC4's client half and making the parent's pass criterion D
(ordering evidence) observable.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — required whether or not Phase B
passes.

## Cross-repo constraint (read first)

This work lands in the **SorraAgents** repository, not this one:

- code: `~/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`
  (`index.ts` adapter + `compaction-bridge.js` pure core),
- tests: `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
- loaded via the symlink `~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge` →
  that directory (verified present 2026-10-31), so no reinstall is needed
  beyond `/reload` inside pi.

The commit hash in SorraAgents must be recorded on this child and on the
parent, so the client half of AC4 is traceable from the LP item. Do not copy
the bridge into this repository.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `compaction-bridge.js` has no logging at all: `handleResponse` returns a
  boolean, `reshape` returns a list or `null`. Neither reports why.
- `index.ts` wires `after_provider_response` and `context` and silently
  returns on a stale ctx / missing signal.
- There is no `ctx.ui` in print or JSON mode (`docs/extensions.md`), so
  `ctx.ui.notify` cannot be the logging channel — headless T2 would lose it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: One line per **captured** signal, emitted from the pure core:
  `compaction-bridge signal captured session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`.
- AC2: One line per **reshape attempt**:
  - applied: `compaction-bridge reshaped <X>-><Y> messages session=<id8>`
    with `Y < X`,
  - not applicable: `compaction-bridge no signal — passthrough session=<id8>`
    (state absent) — the "loaded but idle" line, and
  - anomalous signal (fewer turns than `turnsSummarized`):
    `compaction-bridge reshape refused reason=insufficient_turns session=<id8>`.
- AC3: Exactly one line per event: `handleResponse` logs once whether or not a
  signal was parsed (no-signal case logs at most once per response, and is
  rate-limited to one line per session per turn so an idle session does not
  spam), and `reshape` logs once per `context` event.
- AC4: Works in every pi mode (interactive, RPC, JSON, print): no `ctx.ui`
  dependency. Lines go to **stderr** and, when
  `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG` is set, are appended to that file, one line
  each. The default channel and the optional file path are documented in the
  extension README.
- AC5: No marker text, no message content and no summary body in any line —
  session id (truncated to 8), counts and lengths only.
- AC6: Logging never changes behaviour and never throws: the logger is
  injected into `createCompactionBridge({ log })` with a no-op default, so the
  pure module stays dependency-free and a hostile/throwing logger leaves
  parse/reshape results identical.
- AC7: `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended to assert: the AC1 line
  and its fields; the AC2 applied / passthrough / refused lines; the AC3
  one-line-per-event rule including the idle no-spam case; the AC5 no-body
  guarantee (assert the marker string does not appear in any captured line);
  and AC6 (identical `parseCompactionSignal` / `reshapeContext` results with a
  no-op logger vs a throwing logger). All pre-existing bridge tests stay green
  unmodified.
- AC8: README documents the exact log lines, the `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG`
  variable, and the grep recipe used by T2's criterion D.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `log` option to `createCompactionBridge({ log } = {})` defaulting to a
  no-op; the default writer lives in `index.ts` (adapter layer), keeping
  `compaction-bridge.js` free of `fs`/`process` imports except behind an
  injected function.
- Emit from inside `handleResponse` / `reshape` where the decision is already
  made — no re-parsing, no extra state.
- Idle rate-limiting is one `Set` of session ids already logged for
  passthrough, cleared when a signal is captured for that session (keeps the
  module dependency-free and the logic pure).
- Keep the existing public surface (`handleResponse` boolean, `reshape` list or
  null) unchanged so `index.ts` and the tests need no behavioural edits.
- Run `node --test` for the extension's unit test only via the test skill
  (`/skill:test` scope) — not ad-hoc.

## Deliverables

- `compaction-bridge.js` telemetry + injected logger.
- `index.ts` default logger wiring (stderr + optional file).
- `README.md` log-line documentation.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended coverage.
- SorraAgents commit hash recorded on this item.

**Key Files:**

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/README.md`
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T2 execution child (pass criterion D reads these lines).

data.description:
# Performance metrics in usage report

## Problem statement

The daily usage report presents a lot of raw telemetry but no consolidated
performance scorecard: nothing states which metrics the proxy is held to, what
its historical best is, whether the period met the goal, or why the metric
matters and what levers change it. Targets currently live in scattered,
recently-closed work items, so regressions are only noticed by whoever happens
to read the detailed sections.

## Users

- **Management / stakeholder (primary)** — reads only the first section: a KPI
  scorecard with baseline, target, actual and a met/unmet observation.
- **Operator / SRE (secondary)** — reads the per-metric detail sections to
  understand the calculation, the levers and the trade-offs before changing
  configuration.
- **Agent / audit runners (tertiary)** — consume the same numbers from the
  report and the `--json` output when validating completed performance work.

User stories:

- As a stakeholder I want a single scorecard at the top of the daily report
  showing each performance metric's baseline, target, actual and met/unmet, so I
  can see at a glance whether the proxy is improving without reading raw
  telemetry.
- As a stakeholder I want the three best historical measurements (with their
  dates) behind each target, so I know the target is evidence-based rather than
  arbitrary.
- As an operator I want a detail section per metric covering why it matters, how
  it is calculated, and the levers and trade-offs, so I can decide what to
  change.
- As an operator I want the report to say "insufficient history" instead of a
  false "unmet" when fewer than three measurements exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The daily report's first section after the header is a **Performance metrics
   summary** table with one row per metric and the columns: Metric | Baseline
   (best recorded value + date) | Target (mean of the best 3) | Actual (this
   window) | Result (Met / Unmet / Insufficient history). The table covers the
   ten metrics listed under Desired change.
2. Baseline and target data live in a committed defaults file plus a live state
   file in the report output directory; each run records the window's
   measurement, retains the three best values (direction-aware) with their
   measurement dates, and recomputes the target as the mean of those three. The
   committed file is never mutated at runtime.
3. Met/unmet is direction-aware (higher-is-better vs lower-is-better) and
   compares the window's actual against the target; a metric with fewer than
   three recorded measurements reports **Insufficient history** and never a
   false Met/Unmet.
4. Every metric row in the summary table has a matching detail section in the
   main body stating (a) why the metric matters, (b) how it is calculated
   including its data source, (c) the levers available to change it, and (d) the
   trade-offs of trying to improve it.
5. A one-off backfill seeds the best-3 history from the archived daily reports
   where extraction is reliable; metrics that cannot be parsed start empty and
   accrue history from the first post-ship run. Backfill is idempotent —
   re-running it never duplicates a measurement for the same window.
6. Tests: unit tests cover direction-aware top-3 retention, target = mean of
   best 3, verdict derivation, insufficient-history handling, backfill
   idempotence and the backfill parser against a fixture report; an integration
   test asserts the summary table is the first section with the required
   columns and that each metric has exactly one detail section.
7. `--json` output includes a `performance_metrics` block with the per-metric
   baseline/target/actual/verdict so audits can consume it without parsing
   Markdown.
8. Documentation is updated: `SKILL.md` (new section, unchanged cron
   invocation), `REFERENCE.md` (metric definitions and state-file schema),
   `README.md`.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The existing 05:00 cron invocation must keep working unchanged with default
  flags; the new section is produced by that run.
- The committed defaults file is read-only at runtime; only the live state file
  under `--output-dir` is updated.
- Measurements must remain interpretable across configuration eras: each stored
  measurement records its window and a configuration fingerprint (slot count /
  geometry), and the detail sections flag when the best 3 span different
  configurations.
- Missing or insufficient data degrades to `n/a` / "Insufficient history", never
  to `0` or a misleading verdict — consistent with the report's existing
  never-mislead rule.
- YAML access follows `config_loader.py`'s guarded-import pattern so PyYAML
  stays optional; no new mandatory dependency.
- All user-facing text in UK English.

## Existing state

- `reporting.build_report()` assembles the report; per-topic `_append_*`
  helpers render sections, with the header bullets followed immediately by
  `## Summary by hour`.
- The per-metric inputs are already computed and rendered: `## Local model
  utilization` (busy bounds), `## Fallback reasons`, `## Time to first token`,
  `## Decode speed`, `## Prompt eval speed`, `## Error analysis`, `## Local
  capacity signals` (`slots_stale` target), `## Local contention prediction vs
  reality` (denials/hour and ETA accuracy), and the `Context sizes approaching
  per-slot limits` recommendation.
- Baseline precedents already exist: the hard-coded `CONTENTION_BASELINE` in
  `reporting.py` (sourced from a work-item description) and configurable targets
  such as `capacity_signals.DEFAULT_STALE_RATE_TARGET`.
- `log_parser` already parses `cache_state` / `cached_ratio`, but no report
  section aggregates a prompt-cache hit ratio yet — that aggregation is new.
- 267 archived report directories exist under `~/proxy-usage-reports/` and can
  seed history.
- `analyze_proxy_usage.py` is the CLI; `--json` prints a summary dict.

## Desired change

1. New `performance_metrics.py` module: metric registry (id, label, unit,
   direction, source), state load/save, direction-aware top-3 retention, target
   = mean of the best 3, verdict derivation, and the backfill parser.
2. Ten metrics, each with a summary row and a detail section:
   - **GPU busy / local utilisation (%)** — power-based GPU busy from the
     telemetry sampler, with log-derived local busy as corroboration.
   - **Fallback rate (% of requests)** — plus the dominant fallback reason.
   - **Decode speed** — median tok/s.
   - **Prompt-eval (prefill) speed** — median tok/s.
   - **Time to first token** — local p90 (dispatch → first byte), ms.
   - **Stream error rate** — share of streams ending in error, %.
   - **Context-size pressure** — share of local requests at or above the
     per-slot context threshold, %.
   - **Local prompt-cache hit ratio** — median `cached_ratio` plus warm share
     (new aggregation over already-parsed fields).
   - **Slot-contention denials per hour**.
   - **Prefill-ETA prediction accuracy** — median absolute relative error on
     matched pairs.
3. Summary table rendered as the first section; a **Performance metric details**
   block in the main body with one subsection per metric (importance,
   calculation, levers, trade-offs).
4. Committed defaults `metrics/performance_metrics.yaml` plus live state
   `<output-dir>/performance_metrics_state.yaml`; CLI flags `--metrics-config`,
   `--metrics-state`, `--no-metrics-update` and `--seed-metrics-history` (the
   one-off backfill).
5. The `--json` summary gains a `performance_metrics` block.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the summary table compares the actual against the target (mean
  of the best 3) and shows the single best value as the baseline for context;
  confirmed by the operator during intake.
- **Assumption:** backfill parses only values already rendered in archived
  `report.md` files; metrics whose rendering changed between eras are skipped
  rather than guessed, and gaps accrue from the first post-ship run.
- **Risk — cross-era comparisons:** a best-3 set spanning different slot
  geometries or models compares unlike things. Mitigation: per-measurement
  configuration fingerprint plus an explicit note in the detail section.
- **Risk — history starvation:** with fewer than three measurements the table
  shows "Insufficient history" for days. Mitigation: backfill (AC5) seeds the
  main metrics so the table is useful on the first run.
- **Risk — daily state churn:** writing state into a git-tracked file would
  dirty the tree every night. Mitigation: committed file is defaults-only; the
  mutable state lives under the report output directory.
- **Risk — scope creep:** extra metrics or dashboards will be tempting once the
  registry exists. Mitigation: fixed set of ten for this item; additional
  metrics are filed as linked follow-up work items.
- **Risk — duplication with existing sections:** the detail sections could
  restate the existing data sections. Mitigation: details focus on
  importance/levers/trade-offs and link to the data section rather than
  duplicating tables.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/performance_metrics.py` — New module:
  metric registry, state I/O, top-3/target/verdict logic, backfill parser.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — New
  `_append_performance_metrics_section` (first section) and the detail-block
  builder; consumes the new module.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — Add prompt-cache
  hit-ratio aggregation (median `cached_ratio`, warm/cold share) and expose the
  context-pressure and stream-error-rate figures reusably.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — New CLI
  flags, state-update wiring, `performance_metrics` JSON block,
  `--seed-metrics-history`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/metrics/performance_metrics.yaml` — Committed
  defaults / target template (never written at runtime).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_performance_metrics.py` — Unit
  tests: retention, verdicts, target maths, insufficient history, backfill
  idempotence.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` —
  Integration: report ordering, table columns, one detail section per metric,
  JSON block.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, `README.md` —
  Document the section, the metric definitions, the state-file schema and the
  backfill command.

## Related work

**Directly relevant work items** (the recently completed/closed performance work
this section draws its baselines and metric definitions from):

- LP-0MSAU6MKS008K0RJ — Proxy usage analysis skill: 24h session/fallback log
  analysis with day-night CSVs and recommendation report (the report this item
  extends).
- LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8 — Re-evaluate `session_slot_pool_size` against measured
  GPU busy-time and contention history (busy %, concurrency and queue-timeout
  baselines).
- LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX — Cross-check report slot-time against llama-server eval
  timings (the 25 % divergence threshold precedent).
- LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation history
  (source of the power-based GPU busy figure).
- LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS — Keep local prompt prefixes resident: tenancy hold,
  tenant bound, cache headroom, save/restore reliability (open; its measured
  baseline table — `slots_stale` target < 5 %, GPU busy 66.4 % vs log-derived
  41.7 % — is exactly the shape this scorecard generalises).
- LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S — Usage report eviction metrics and triage rule (the
  closest precedent: new report section + `--json` keys + docs + tests).
- LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ — Investigate what happens if I switch to a single slot
  (slot geometry era boundaries that the configuration fingerprint must record).
- LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES — Add session + attempt + budget evidence to Fallback
  triggered log lines (fallback attribution used by the fallback-rate metric).
- LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN — Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx
  (open; the >60 % busy gate shows why a fixed target must be era-aware).

**Potentially related docs** (paths):

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — CLI usage, cron line and
  interpretation guide that must document the new section.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` — metric source-of-truth
  reference; the natural home for the metric definitions and state-file schema.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/README.md` — pipeline overview.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — report assembly,
  `CONTENTION_BASELINE` and `summary_to_json` (the baseline/JSON precedent).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/capacity_signals.py` —
  `DEFAULT_STALE_RATE_TARGET`, the existing configurable-target precedent.
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/` — 267 archived daily reports, the backfill source.

**Automated find-related report** (weak matches; recorded for traceability):

- LP-0MO6EXFG7004JGPG — Telemetry and observability for session metrics
  (completed).
- LP-0MPYBSKQV0054699 — Docs: llama local status endpoint (completed).
- LP-0MQJGW3LO000H14M — Test: Prometheus token-rate metric verification
  (completed).

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q:** Where should baselines and targets come from? (options: derive from
  historical reports / hard-code in reporting code / dedicated baselines file /
  reuse embedded baselines) — **Answer (operator):** "C (keep the 3 best for each
  metric, the best being the one we compare against, along with the dates they
  were measured) + D" — i.e. a dedicated file holding the three best measurements
  with dates, plus reuse of the baselines already embedded in
  `reporting.py` where they exist. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** What is the primary audience? — **Answer (operator):** "B" —
  management/stakeholders who need high-level KPIs. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Auto-generated by the daily cron or separate on-demand generation? —
  **Answer (operator):** "A" — auto-generated with the daily cron report. Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q:** Where do the target numbers come from? — **Answer (operator):** "C - but
  the target should be the average of the best three". Source: interactive reply.
  Research: `reporting.py` already hard-codes `CONTENTION_BASELINE` (sourced from
  a work-item description) and `capacity_signals.DEFAULT_STALE_RATE_TARGET`
  supplies a configurable target; the new file generalises this precedent.
- **Q:** Which metrics should the summary table include? (proposed set) —
  **Answer (operator):** "A" — all proposed metrics: local busy / GPU
  utilisation, fallback rate and dominant reasons, decode speed, prompt-eval
  speed, TTFT, stream error rate, context-size pressure, cache hit ratio,
  contention denials per hour, admission/prefill-ETA accuracy. Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q:** Should the metrics file be committed or report-directory only? —
  **Answer (operator):** "A" — committed template/config in the skill plus the
  live updated copy in the report directory. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** How should the best-3 history be seeded? — **Answer (operator):** "C" —
  backfill where extraction is reliable, otherwise start recording from the first
  run. Source: interactive reply. Research: 267 archived report directories
  under `~/proxy-usage-reports/` supply the backfill source; `report.md` renders
  busy %, fallback rate, decode/prompt-eval medians, TTFT percentiles, error
  counts and contention denials in a stable table shape.
- **Q:** Confirm met/unmet semantics? — **Answer (operator):** "A" — met/unmet
  compares the period's actual against the target (mean of the best 3); the
  baseline column shows the single best recorded value for context. Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Decision (agent, recorded for review):** the metric detail sections are
  grouped in one **Performance metric details** block immediately after the
  summary table rather than interleaved with the existing data sections, so each
  metric's importance/levers/trade-offs read together and the existing data
  sections keep their current order. Rationale: the requirement places the
  summary first and the details "in the main body"; a single block avoids
  scattering ten new subsections through a 900-line report.

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/test_rebuild_and_restart_mtp.py::test_rebuild_failure_does_not_abort_restart
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
assert start_marker.exists(), "stack was NOT restarted despite rebuild failure"
E AssertionError: stack was NOT restarted despite rebuild failure
E assert False
E + where False = exists()
E + where exists = PosixPath("/tmp/pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-1986/test_rebuild_failure_does_not_0/start-proxy.marker").exists
tests/test_rebuild_and_restart_mtp.py:111: AssertionError
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k tests/test_rebuild_and_restart_mtp.py::test_rebuild_failure_does_not_abort_restart` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/test_rebuild_and_restart_mtp.py::test_rebuild_failure_does_not_abort_restart` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Diagnosis (implement session)

**Root cause — test/implementation race, not a product bug.** `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh`'s
`restart_stack()` launches the restart in the background:

```bash
nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart &>/tmp/mtp-proxy-restart.log &
```

The test then asserts `start_marker.exists()` immediately after `subprocess.run` returns, with no
synchronisation. Under full-suite load the background job has not yet written the marker, so the
assertion fails even though the restart was launched. It passes standalone and when the whole file
runs alone; it fails inside the 7 800-test full suite (observed 2026-11-04, 1 failed / 7 806 passed).

**Fix:** bound the wait in the test — poll for the marker (and the re-deploy marker) with a short
timeout instead of asserting on a single immediate check. The production script is correct: a
detached restart must not block the one-shot rebuild wrapper.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_rebuild_and_restart_mtp.py` — add a bounded wait helper and use it before each
  background-restart assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria (revised)

1. `tests/test_rebuild_and_restart_mtp.py::test_rebuild_failure_does_not_abort_restart` and its
   siblings pass reliably, including under full-suite load.
2. The assertions still prove behaviour (restart invoked with `--restart`, one rebuild invocation,
   exit code 1) — the wait only removes the race, it does not weaken the check.
3. Full project test suite passes.

# `available_slots` contradicts its own `slots[]` in `/llama/local/status`

**Priority:** high - dangerous payload, but not currently what blocks scheduling.
**Type:** bug · **Risk:** High · **Effort:** S

## Impact

A single response from `GET /llama/local/status` asserts availability and
unavailability at the same time. A client that trusts the summary field
over-dispatches; a client that trusts the detail correctly refuses. A human
reading the summary concludes "GPU idle, dispatcher broken" - the opposite of
the truth.

This was the trap in our own investigation: an earlier read of the admission
guard's `busy_slots=0 in_flight_prefills=0 free_slot=true` produced the
conclusion "the GPU was idle and the request was refused anyway". Those fields
derive from the same frozen snapshot, so the GPU state was **unobservable**, not
idle.

## Evidence (live, 2026-11-04 08:42)

Same response body:

```json
{
  "slots_stale": true,
  "slots_detail_stale": true,
  "slots_snapshot_source": "snapshot",
  "slots_snapshot_age_seconds": 29825.67,
  "total_slots": 2,
  "available_slots": 2,
  "capacity_hint": "idle",
  "local_abandoned_slots": 2,
  "local_in_flight_requests": 0,
  "slots": [
    {"slot_id": 0, "is_processing": true, "abandoned": true,
     "abandonment_reason": "measured_cache_deficit", "lease_state": "generating",
     "phase": "decode", "n_decoded": 65},
    {"slot_id": 1, "is_processing": true, "abandoned": true,
     "lease_state": "generating", "phase": "decode", "n_decoded": 368}
  ]
}
```

`available_slots: 2` while both listed slots are `is_processing: true`. The
`n_decoded` values (65 and 368) are frozen - unchanged across polls 8 hours
apart. `capacity_hint: "idle"` and `local_idle_seconds` keep climbing while two
slots are simultaneously reported as generating.

## Root cause

The summary fields (`available_slots`, `capacity_hint`, `local_idle_seconds`) are
derived independently of the `slots[]` array and are not invalidated when that
array is stale. Nothing enforces the cross-field invariant
`available_slots == count(slots[] where is_processing == false)`.

## Change

1. **Derive the summary from the detail.** `available_slots` is computed from
   `slots[]` by construction, never from a separate counter.
2. **Never assert availability from a stale list.** When
   `slots_stale == true`, the summary fields must not claim capacity: publish
   `available_slots: null` (or `0` plus an explicit `availability_unknown: true`)
   and forbid `capacity_hint: "idle"`.
3. **Stop `local_idle_seconds` climbing** while any slot reports
   `is_processing: true`.
4. **Attribute the abandonment to availability** - `local_abandoned_slots: 2`
   must reduce availability rather than sit beside `available_slots: 2`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The cross-field invariant holds by construction and is pinned by a test
      over a matrix of slot states: `available_slots == count(slots[] where
      is_processing == false)`.
- [ ] With a fixture where both snapshot slots are `is_processing: true` and
      `abandoned: true`, the payload reports `available_slots == 0` (or `null`
      with an explicit unknown flag) and `capacity_hint != "idle"`.
- [ ] With `slots_stale == true`, no summary field asserts availability, and a
      test asserts the summary cannot contradict the detail for **any**
      staleness/staleness-reason combination.
- [ ] `local_idle_seconds` does not increase while any slot reports
      `is_processing: true` (test advances the clock and asserts the field
      holds).
- [ ] `/llama/local/status` schema stays backward compatible for the field
      names already consumed by clients (`slots_stale`, `slots_detail_stale`,
      `available_slots`, `capacity_hint`, `total_slots`); any change to the
      meaning of a field is documented in the payload schema notes.
- [ ] Live verification recorded: on the repaired host, a response serialised in
      the same conditions shows the summary agreeing with the detail.
- [ ] Full test suite green via the test skill.
data.title: available_slots contradicts its own slots[] in /llama/local/status
